content: To search for a specific article containing a particular word, you should type the desired word or topic into the search box located on the left-hand side of the screen and then press the Search button. Next to the Search button, you will also find a Go button. The Go button is designed to display only pages with titles that exactly match the word or phrase you entered. This makes the Go function a more restrictive search tool, as it lists only pages with the specified name. If you already know the exact title of the page you are looking for, the Go button allows you to navigate directly to that page without needing to follow any links. Another method of searching involves using categories. For example, you can click on a category such as Pulmonary or Nephrology on the main homepage. This will display a list of all articles that are organized under that specific category. If you want to see a complete list of all available categories, you can click on Special:categories. To view a list of all pages on WikiDoc, you can either type Special:Allpages into the search menu or click on the Table of Contents button located above and to the left. Searching Tips: 1. Avoid using short and common words: If your search includes common stop words such as the, one, your, more, right, while, when, who, which, such, every, about, or onto, your search may fail to return results. Similarly, short numbers or words that appear on a large proportion of pages will also not be found. In such cases, remove these words and try the search again. For more information, refer to Help:Common words. Note that searching for a combination of a common word and another term (e.g., not) may result in a database query syntax error due to a software bug. 2. Searches are case-insensitive: For example, searching for acute MI, Acute MI, or ACUTE MI will yield the same results. 3. Do not use phrases: WikiDoc does not support searching for exact phrases. If you enclose a phrase in double quotation marks (e.g., can of tuna), the search will return all pages containing the individual words can, of, and tuna, rather than the exact phrase. 4. Avoid using regular expressions or wildcards: You cannot use symbols like ? or in your search. For instance, if you want to search for pages containing boat or boats, you should type boat or boats instead. 5. Do not search for words in single quotes: If a word appears in a page with single quotes, you must include the quotes in your search to find it. However, this is rarely desirable. It is better to use double quotes in pages to avoid this issue. Note that an apostrophe is treated as a single quote. For example, Mu'ammar can only be found if you search for it exactly as written. However, words with an apostrophe followed by s (e.g., doctor's) can also be found by searching for the word without the apostrophe and s (e.g., doctor). 6. Do not use the underscore character (_) as a space: The underscore is not equivalent to a space. If you include an underscore in the URL, the search will look for words that contain actual underscores in those positions. 7. Be patient with search updates: Recent changes to pages may not be immediately reflected in search results due to delays in updating the search index. This is done for reasons of efficiency and prioritization. Search Options: 1. Browsing image filenames: To search for image titles, use Special:Imagelist. Searching within the image namespace will search the descriptions of images, which are the initial parts of the image pages. 2. Wikitext is searched: The search function looks at the wikitext (the source text visible in the edit box). This is important for elements like piped links, interlanguage links, and special characters. For example, if the character ê is encoded as ê in the wikitext, it will be found by searching for ecirc. 3. Highlighting search terms: Portions of matching pages that contain the searched terms will be displayed, with the terms highlighted in red. You can adjust the number of lines shown and the amount of text per line in your preferences. For example, if you search for book, the results will include only pages containing the word book, not pages with only the word books. However, on pages containing both book and books, the book portion of the word books will also be highlighted.
